_description: Active inductance probes. These are reasoning trap questions sent with the ORIGINAL clean image. The question looks simple but requires deeper reasoning to answer correctly. A naive/surface-level reading gives the wrong answer.

probes.question: Най-големият дял в кръговата диаграма е обозначен с 25. Означава ли това, че този сектор представлява 25% от отговорите?
probes.question_english: The largest slice in the pie chart is labeled 25. Does this mean that this sector represents 25% of the responses?
probes.expected_answer: No. The values (10, 24, 25, 8, 20) are raw counts, not percentages. They sum to 87, not 100. The 25 slice actually represents approximately 28.7% of responses (25/87).
probes.trap: Values look like percentages but are actually counts — they don't sum to 100
probes.what_it_tests: Can the model detect that displayed values are raw counts, not percentages, by checking if they sum to 100?
probes.correct_reasoning: Model must notice values sum to 87 not 100, therefore they are counts not percentages

probes.question: The outer ring has two small adjacent slices showing 7.0% and 5.0%. The legend lists Std values in order: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94 from darkest to lightest blue. Which Std value does the 7.0% slice belong to?
probes.question_english: The outer ring has two small adjacent slices showing 7.0% and 5.0%. The legend lists Std values in order: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94 from darkest to lightest blue. Which Std value does the 7.0% slice belong to?
probes.expected_answer: Std: 0.94. The 7.0% slice is the lightest blue (rightmost in the outer ring), which corresponds to Std: 0.94 (lightest in the legend).
probes.trap: The two small slices look similar — model must use color gradient to distinguish them
probes.what_it_tests: Can the model use color gradient ordering in the legend to correctly map visually similar slices to their correct categories?
probes.naive_answer: Std: 0.82 (just guessing one of the two)
probes.correct_reasoning: Model must match the color shade of the 7.0% slice to the legend gradient — lighter = higher Std value

probes.question: At 80% sparsity, the two bars appear to be roughly the same height visually. Is the actual difference in perplexity between Per-Layer and Per-Output small or large?
probes.question_english: At 80% sparsity, the two bars appear to be roughly the same height visually. Is the actual difference in perplexity between Per-Layer and Per-Output small or large?
probes.expected_answer: The difference is very large. The y-axis uses a logarithmic scale (10^1, 10^2, 10^3). Although the bars look similar in height, they represent values differing by hundreds on the actual scale.
probes.trap: On a log scale, visually similar bar heights can represent enormous actual differences
probes.what_it_tests: Can the model recognize the logarithmic y-axis scale and understand that visual proximity on a log scale does not mean numerical proximity?
probes.naive_answer: The difference is small — the bars look almost the same height
probes.correct_reasoning: Model must identify the y-axis as logarithmic and understand that equal visual distances on a log scale represent multiplicative, not additive, differences
